limits.title: What „sent" means — and what the phone cannot do
limits.sent: Sent ≠ the lamp worked. Android only confirms that the BLE advertisement started and was stopped. Whether the lamp heard it, you check yourself (the „Yes/No" buttons in the console).
limits.noAddress: Choosing a device does not address a lamp. A BLE advertisement reaches everything in range. Which lamp switches on is decided by the bytes in the packet (identifier, counter — depending on the manufacturer), not by the name or number here.
limits.noSpoof: The remote's address is not faked. The phone transmits from its own (random) address; a normal app cannot change it. If the lamp checks the sender's address, the packet alone is not enough.
limits.replay: Replay protection. If the remote changes a counter or code on every press, a recorded packet may be rejected.
limits.timing: Timings are approximate. A packet goes out at most every 100 ms — Android does not transmit faster (the pause slider can only make that gap longer); starting and switching between frames take tens of milliseconds. Gaps of a few ms as in the remote are not possible — the console shows how long it really took.
limits.makerOnly: Only manufacturer data (0xFF) is sent unchanged. Android arranges other structures (name, flags, UUID) its own way — such packets are rejected with an explanation, not silently changed.
limits.power: The phone transmits at „high" power, not connectable; 31 bytes is the limit of a legacy advertisement.

json.title: Lamps — import and export (JSON)
json.lead: Devices with signals, timers and the button pace — a backup, a move to another account or timers prepared by AI. Whatever has an „id” from the export is changed in place; whatever has none is created. Only „remove”: true deletes.
json.partialMade: Saved {done} of {total} changes, then: {problem} New entries that were already created would be created a second time if the same text were imported again — download a fresh export first.
